questions.title: Generator Payment Options, School Sports Uniform, and Unemployment Rates

subQuestions.questionText: A generator is a useful device that can be used to provide an alternate source of electricity during a power outage. Payment options shown: Cash price R10 999 (including 15% VAT); Hire-purchase: Deposit 10%, Instalment R534,14 pm × 24 months, Interest rate 14,75%; Online credit (via Mobicred): Instalment R1 006 pm × 12 months, Interest rate 9,76%. Give TWO payment options for this generator.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any two of: Hire-purchase / Online credit (Mobicred) / Cash price.
Mark 1: 1A first method
Mark 2: 1A second method

subQuestions.questionText: Define hire-purchase within the given context.
subQuestions.memoText:
You buy the generator at a monthly instalment. Only after your final instalment do you own the generator.
Mark 1-2: 2A correct explanation (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the interest rate if the generator was bought on hire-purchase.
subQuestions.memoText:
14,75%
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct percentage (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total cost of the generator using Mobicred.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total cost = R1 006 × 12 = R12 072
Mark 1: 1MA multiply by 12
Mark 2: 1A simplification (R12 072)

subQuestions.questionText: A 12,5% discount is given on the cash price. Calculate the amount of discount given if the generator is purchased for cash.
subQuestions.memoText:
Discount = $\frac{12,5}{100} \times R10\,999 = R1\,374,88$
Mark 1: 1MA calculating 12,5%
Mark 2: 1A amount discount (R1 374,88)
Accept: R1 374,90 OR R1 375

subQuestions.questionText: Name the type of interest charged if the generator is bought on hire-purchase.
subQuestions.memoText:
Simple Interest
Mark 1-2: 2A simple interest (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 1 shows prices of school sport uniform with percentage (%) change in price (Sport shirt -1,1; Sport shorts -17,4; Sport skirt -6,7; Tracksuit top 42,7; Tracksuit pants 122,2; Sport socks 10,1; Cap 90,1). Arrange (in ascending order) the % change in price.
subQuestions.memoText:
Ascending order: -17,4%; -6,7%; -1,1%; 10,1%; 42,7%; 90,1%; 122,2%
Mark 1: 1RT correct values
Mark 2: 1A ascending order

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the third most expensive item in 2022. (2022 prices: Sport shirt R265, Sport shorts R177, Sport skirt R232, Tracksuit top R382, Tracksuit pants R195, Sport socks R53,50, Cap R171)
subQuestions.memoText:
Sport skirt
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct item (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the difference in price of a cap bought in 2022 compared to 2021. (2021: R89,95; 2022: R171,00)
subQuestions.memoText:
Difference = R171,00 - R89,95 = R81,05
Mark 1: 1MA subtracting correct values
Mark 2: 1A difference (R81,05)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the total cost of the school sport uniform in 2021. (2021 prices: Sport shirt R267,92; Sport shorts R214,17; Sport skirt R248,70; Tracksuit top R267,78; Tracksuit pants R87,75; Sport socks R48,58; Cap R89,95)
subQuestions.memoText:
Total cost = R267,92 + R214,17 + R248,70 + R267,78 + R87,75 + R48,58 + R89,95 = R1 224,85
Mark 1: 1MA adding correct values
Mark 2: 1CA simplification (R1 224,85)
CA only if 1 value omitted

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE other item NOT listed in the table that John's daughter might need in order to play for the school hockey team.
subQuestions.memoText:
Shinpads OR Hockey shoes (Any hockey related equipment)
Mark 1-2: 2A correct item (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 1.3.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The line graph shows official and expanded unemployment rates for 2021 for all the provinces in South Africa. Write down the province with the highest expanded unemployment rate. (Expanded rates: EC 49,6; FS 43,4; GP 41,6; MP 47,6; NW 47,2; KZN 46,4; LP 49,5; WC 27,9; NC 42,2)
subQuestions.memoText:
EC (Eastern Cape)
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct province (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 1.3.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down the province with the smallest difference between the official unemployment rate and the expanded unemployment rate.
subQuestions.memoText:
WC (Western Cape)
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct province (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine which province represents the modal official unemployment rate. (Official rates: EC 43,8; FS 35,6; GP 34,4; MP 33,5; NW 32,2; KZN 30,5; LP 29,4; WC 23,7; NC 23,4)
subQuestions.memoText:
No province / No Mode
Mark 1-2: 2A correct solution (2 marks)
(All values are different so there is no mode.)

subQuestions.questionText: The total labour force for the Free State (FS) was 918 000 in 2021. Calculate the number of officially unemployed people in the Free State.
subQuestions.memoText:
Number of unemployed people = $35,6\% \times 918\,000 = 326\,808$
Mark 1: 1RT correct % (35,6%)
Mark 2: 1MA calculating percentage
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (326 808)

questions.title: Guesthouse Booking, Refurbishing Cars, and Compound Interest

subQuestions.questionText: Roadside Tours and Travel Agency made a booking at a guesthouse for 36 work colleagues to attend a conference in Upington. Use ANNEXURE A (invoice). Write down the address of the guesthouse.
subQuestions.memoText:
125 Bossie Street, Upington
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct address (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The accommodation cost includes 15% VAT. Determine (excluding VAT) the price for a person per night in a 2-bed room. (Price including VAT = R900)
subQuestions.memoText:
Excluding VAT = $R900 \times \frac{100}{115} = R782,6086957 \approx R782,61$
Mark 1: 1RT correct accommodation (R900)
Mark 2: 1MA excluding calculation
Mark 3: 1A simplification (R782,61)
Alternative: $\frac{R900}{1,15} = R782,61$
Alternative: VAT = R900 × (15÷115) = R117,39; Excluding VAT = R900 - R117,39 = R782,61

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the missing value C, the total for the 4-bed room. (Total invoice R75 040; other accommodation values R28 800 + R5 760 + R6 480, or 4-bed rate R850 × 2 nights × 20 guests)
subQuestions.memoText:
C = R75 040,00 - (R28 800 + R5 760 + R6 480) = R34 000
OR C = R850 × 2 × 20 = R34 000
Mark 1: 1MA correct values used
Mark 2: 1CA simplification (R34 000)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine (in simplified form) the ratio of the number of guests booked in the 2-bed rooms to the number of guests booked in the 4-bed rooms.
subQuestions.memoText:
Number of guests in 4-bed rooms = R34 000 ÷ (2 × 850) = 20
Number of guests in 2-bed rooms = R28 800 ÷ (2 × 900) = 16
Ratio = 16 : 20 = 4 : 5
Mark 1: 1MCA dividing and multiplying
Mark 2: 1CA simplification (20)
Mark 3: 1MCA dividing and multiplying
Mark 4: 1CA number of guests in 2-bed accommodation (16)
Mark 5: 1MCA ratio in correct order (16 : 20)
Mark 6: 1CA simplification (4 : 5)
CA from Question 2.1.3
Alternative: 36 - 16 = 20 (using total of 36 guests)

subQuestions.questionText: Two work colleagues who booked the 2-bed rooms cancelled as follows: One cancelled at 11:00, while the other one cancelled at 15:00 on the check-in date. Their meal cost will be fully refunded, while the accommodation costs will be refunded according to the conditions of the cancellation policy stated in ANNEXURE A. The tour operator stated that the refund would be less than R2 500. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether this statement is CORRECT.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cost of one guest in 2-bed room = 2 × R900 = R1 800
Refund for cancelling before check-in time (75%) = $\frac{75}{100} \times R1\,800 = R1\,350$
Refund for cancelling after check-in time (25%) = $\frac{25}{100} \times R1\,800 = R450$
Refund for meals = 4 × R80 + 4 × R90 = R680
Total Refund = R450 + R1 350 + R680 = R2 480
Statement is CORRECT (R2 480 < R2 500)
Mark 1: 1A total accommodation (R1 800)
Mark 2: 1MCA calculating 75%
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (R1 350)
Mark 4: 1CA second accommodation refund (R450)
Mark 5: 1A meal refund (R680)
Mark 6: 1CA total refund (R2 480)
Mark 7: 1O conclusion (CORRECT)

subQuestions.questionText: Niel owns a panel beating business. He specialises in buying accident-damaged cars which he refurbishes for resale. Costs to refurbish a 2019 model Renault Kwid bought for R50 000: Cost of panel beating and painting R22 000; Cost of fixing minor engine faults R3 682,50; Valet R450,00. Calculate the total cost of buying and refurbishing the accident-damaged car.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cost to fix the vehicle = R50 000 + R22 000 + R3 682,50 + R450 = R76 132,50
Mark 1: 1MA adding all values
Mark 2: 1CA correct answer (R76 132,50)
AO (answer only) accepted

subQuestions.questionText: Niel normally sells the refurbished car at 65% of the cost price of a brand new similar model car. The cost price of a brand new similar model car is R145 900. Niel stated that he will make a profit of more than R20 000 when he sells the refurbished car. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
Selling price = $\frac{65}{100} \times R145\,900 = R94\,835$
Profit = R94 835 - R76 132,50 = R18 702,50
Not VALID (profit is less than R20 000)
Mark 1: 1MA percentage calculation
Mark 2: 1A correct answer (R94 835)
Mark 3: 1MCA subtracting values
Mark 4: 1CA simplification (R18 702,50)
Mark 5: 1O conclusion (Not valid)
CA from Question 2.2.1

subQuestions.questionText: Niel invests R15 000 of his total profit in a bank which offers him the following interest rates: 6,25% interest compounded yearly for the first year and an interest rate of 6,95% compounded yearly for the second year. Calculate the total interest that Niel's investment would earn at the end of the second year.
subQuestions.memoText:
Interest year 1 = R15 000 × 6,25% = R937,50
Amount after one year = R15 000 + R937,50 = R15 937,50
Interest year 2 = R15 937,50 × 6,95% = R1 107,66
Total Interest = R937,50 + R1 107,66 = R2 045,16
Mark 1: 1A interest (R937,50)
Mark 2: 1MA adding interest
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (R15 937,50)
Mark 4: 1CA simplification (R1 107,66)
Mark 5: 1MCA adding values
Mark 6: 1CA simplification (R2 045,16)
Alternative: $R15\,000 \times 1,0625 \times 1,0695 = R17\,045,16$; Interest = R17 045,16 - R15 000 = R2 045,16

questions.title: Motor Holdings Employees and Box-and-Whisker Plots

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 2 in ANNEXURE B shows the number of people employed at Motor Holdings (MH) in August 2020 and 2019. In August 2020, the company had 41 motor dealerships and a head office. Write down the total number of semi-skilled workers employed by MH during August 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
537
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct value (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the difference in the total number of employees from August 2019 to August 2020. (Total 2019: 2 828; Total 2020: 2 163)
subQuestions.memoText:
Difference = 2 163 - 2 828 = -665
Mark 1: 1RT correct values chosen
Mark 2: 1CA simplification (-665)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the number of staff with disabilities employed in 2020 as a percentage of all the employees in 2020. (Staff with disabilities = 34)
subQuestions.memoText:
% employees with disabilities = $\frac{34}{2\,163} \times 100\% = 1,572\%$
Mark 1: 1RT correct values chosen
Mark 2: 1MCA calculate %
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (1,572%)
Accept: 1,6% and 1,57%
CA from Question 3.1.2

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the average number of employees per dealership if 1,5% of the total number of employees worked at the head office in August 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
% employees at head office = 1,5% × 2 163 = 32,445
Number of employees in motor dealerships = 2 163 - 32,445 = 2 130,555
Average per dealership = 2 130,555 ÷ 41 = 51,9647...
Mark 1: 1A employees at head office (32,445)
Mark 2: 1MCA subtracting
Mark 3: 1CA employees at branches (2 130,555)
Mark 4: 1MCA average concept
Mark 5: 1CA simplification (51,9647)
NPR. Accept: 51,96 / 51,97 / 52 / 51
Alternative: 100% - 1,5% = 98,5%; 98,5% × 2 163 = 2 130,555; ÷ 41 = 51,9647

subQuestions.questionText: Determine (as a percentage rounded off to THREE decimal places) the probability of randomly choosing a coloured female from the list of employees in August 2020. (Number of coloured females = 54)
subQuestions.memoText:
% coloured females = $\frac{54}{2\,163} \times 100\% = 2,497\%$
Mark 1: 1RT correct values
Mark 2: 1MA probability concept
Mark 3: 1R rounded answer (2,497%)
CA from Question 3.1.2

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: ANNEXURE C shows in percentages box and whisker plots of the unemployment rate for all the provinces in South Africa from 2019 to 2021. Determine the lower quartile for 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
Lower Quartile = 21
Mark 1-2: 2RT finding correct value (2 marks)
Accept: above 20 - less than 22

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the 75th percentile for 2019.
subQuestions.memoText:
75th percentile = 28,2
Mark 1-2: 2RT finding correct value (2 marks)
Accept: above 28 - 29

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the median for 2021.
subQuestions.memoText:
Median = 31,5
Mark 1-2: 2RT finding correct value (2 marks)
Accept: 30,5 - 32,5

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why it could be said that the unemployment rate was at its highest in 2021.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any two of the following:
- 50% of all the provinces had an unemployment rate of higher than 31,75%
- The median of the data is the highest in 2021
- The maximum value is the highest in 2021
- The box and whisker indicates a higher unemployment rate
- Q3 is higher in 2021 than in 2020 and 2019
Mark 1-2: 2O first explanation
Mark 3-4: 2O second explanation

questions.title: Bank Fees, Income Tax, and Budget Pie Charts

subQuestions.questionText: Katlego is employed at a school by the Presidential Youth Employment Initiative (PYEI). He earns a salary of R4 000 per month. He has a NEDBANK Pay-as-you-use Account but is thinking of changing to a CAPITEC Global One Account. TABLE 3 shows the transactional fees for the two banks. Give ONE reason why banks charge more for branch deposits than ATM deposits.
subQuestions.memoText:
Possible answers:
- Banks are discouraging clients to go to the branch to reduce the number of people visiting the bank.
- Banks have to pay employees working in the bank.
- To reduce the wage bill.
Mark 1-2: 2A explanation (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the difference in cost of an external debit order using a Nedbank Pay-as-you-use account and a Capitec Global One account. (Nedbank: R5,00; Capitec: R1,50)
subQuestions.memoText:
Difference = R5,00 - R1,50 = R3,50
Mark 1: 1RT correct values
Mark 2: 1A simplification (R3,50)

subQuestions.questionText: Katlego had the following monthly transactions on his bank statement: Two external debit orders; One cash withdrawal of R1 500 at own bank ATM; One cash withdrawal of R450 at another bank ATM; One Send cash transaction of R1 500 to his mother. The CAPITEC banking fees for the listed transactions are R45,00. Katlego states that he would have saved R20,50 on bank fees if he banked with CAPITEC rather than NEDBANK. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether Katlego's statement is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
Nedbank Pay-as-you-use:
Transaction cost = 2 × R5,00 + 2 × R9,00 + R11 + 5 × R2,30 + R15 = R65,50
Difference = R65,50 - R45,00 = R20,50
His statement is VALID.
Mark 1: 1A debit order fees (2 × R5,00)
Mark 2: 1A cash withdrawal own ATM (2 × R9,00)
Mark 3: 1SF correct formula (R11 + 5 × R2,30 for other ATM)
Mark 4: 1A cash send cost (R15)
Mark 5: 1CA simplification (R65,50)
Mark 6: 1CA subtracting (R20,50)
Mark 7: 1O valid

subQuestions.questionText: Katlego (who is 24 years old) has two jobs: one at the PYEI and the other at a retail store. He earned a combined annual taxable income of R87 329 for the 2021/2022 tax year. Use TABLE 4 (tax rates: R0-R216 200 = 18% of each R1; primary rebate R15 714). Calculate Katlego's annual tax payable for the 2021/2022 tax year.
subQuestions.memoText:
Annual tax payable before primary rebate = R87 329 × 18% = R15 719,22
Annual tax payable after primary rebate = R15 719,22 - R15 714 = R5,22
Mark 1: 1MA correct tax bracket
Mark 2: 1CA simplification (R15 719,22)
Mark 3: 1MCA subtracting primary rebate
Mark 4: 1CA simplification (R5,22)

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term tax rebate.
subQuestions.memoText:
The discount SARS gives to tax payers.
OR: Rebate is a tax relief given to tax payers.
Mark 1-2: 2O tax discount (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Show that the tax threshold for age 65 to age 74 in the table is CORRECT. (Threshold: R135 150; Primary rebate R15 714; Secondary rebate R8 613; Tax rate 18%)
subQuestions.memoText:
Total rebate = R15 714 + R8 613 = R24 327
Tax threshold = R24 327 ÷ 18% = R135 150
Mark 1: 1RT correct value (R15 714)
Mark 2: 1RT correct value (R8 613)
Mark 3: 1MA adding correct values
Mark 4: 1MCA simplification (R24 327)
Mark 5: 1MCA dividing by 18% (R135 150)
Alternative: R135 150 × 18% = R24 327; R24 327 - (R15 714 + R8 613) = R0

subQuestions.questionText: Katlego moved into a rented flat. Two pie charts show a comparison of his monthly budget with his parents' combined monthly budget. (Categories: A=Food and electricity, B=Insurance, C=Clothing and personal care, D=Communication, E=Savings, F=Other). Name ONE other type of graph that could be used to display the data above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Compound / dual / multiple / stacked bar graph
OR: Line Graph
Mark 1-2: 2A graph (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the missing value D in Katlego's monthly budget. (Katlego's budget: A=40%, B=5%, C=30%, D=?, E=5%, F=5%)
subQuestions.memoText:
D = 100% - (40% + 5% + 30% + 5% + 5%) = 15%
Mark 1: 1MA subtracting from 100%
Mark 2: 1CA simplification (15%)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine (as a decimal) the probability of randomly choosing an item in the parents' budget which is NOT savings. (Parents' budget: A=30%, B=15%, C=10%, D=10%, E=15%, F=20%)
subQuestions.memoText:
P(not savings) = 100% - 15% = 85% = 0,85
OR P(not savings) = 30% + 15% + 10% + 10% + 20% = 85% = 0,85
Mark 1: 1RT correct percentages
Mark 2: 1CA simplification (85%)
Mark 3: 1C converting to decimal (0,85)

questions.title: Brazil Agricultural Production and International Trade

subQuestions.questionText: The graph shows the percentage of the gross value of production of the main agricultural products in Brazil. The percentage gross value of production of bananas decreased from 2020 to 2021. Identify the agricultural product that had the largest increase from 2020 to 2021. (2020 vs 2021: Soybean 26,01 vs 25,98; Sugarcane 18,17 vs 16,60; Corn 10,05 vs 11,91; Coffee Beans 8,92 vs 9,33; Orange 6,67 vs 6,22; Banana 4,51 vs B; Cottonseed 1,76 vs 3,95)
subQuestions.memoText:
Cottonseed
Mark 1-2: 2RT reading from graph (2 marks)
(Cottonseed had the largest increase: from 1,76% to 3,95%)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the total amount (in US$) that coffee contributed in 2020. (Total gross value for 2020 was US$110 322 million; coffee = 8,92%)
subQuestions.memoText:
Coffee contribution = $\frac{8,92}{100} \times \$110\,322$ million = $9 840,7224 million
Mark 1: 1RT reading from graph (8,92)
Mark 2: 1MA multiplying with total amount
Mark 3: 1CA simplification ($9 840,7224 million / $9 840 722 400)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the probability of randomly choosing potatoes as an agricultural product from the data above.
subQuestions.memoText:
0 OR 0% OR Impossible
Mark 1-2: 2A correct probability (2 marks)
(Potatoes are not listed in the data, so probability is 0.)

subQuestions.questionText: The gross value for the production of soybeans was US$32 201 billion in 2021. Determine (in billions) the amount for the production of corn in 2021. (Soybean = 25,98%; Corn = 11,91%)
subQuestions.memoText:
25,98% = $32 201 billion
Total amount = $\frac{100}{25,98} \times \$32\,201$ billion = $123 945 billion
Amount for corn = $\frac{11,91}{100} \times \$123\,945$ billion = $14 761,890300 billion
Mark 1: 1RT correct percentage (25,98)
Mark 2: 1MA working with correct %
Mark 3: 1CA simplification ($123 945 billion)
Mark 4: 1RT correct % (11,91)
Mark 5: 1CA simplification ($14 761,89 billion)
Alternative ratio method: $\frac{11,91}{25,98} \times \$32\,201 = \$14\,761,89$ billion

subQuestions.questionText: The average percentage contribution for the seven agricultural products was 11,15% in 2021. Determine the percentage contribution of bananas (B) in 2021.
subQuestions.memoText:
$11,15 = \frac{25,98 + 16,60 + 11,91 + 9,33 + 6,22 + B + 3,95}{7}$
$11,15 = \frac{73,99 + B}{7}$
$78,05 = 73,99 + B$
$B = 78,05 - 73,99 = 4,06$
Mark 1: 1MA concept of mean
Mark 2: 1MA adding values (73,99)
Mark 3: 1S simplification (78,05)
Mark 4: 1MCA changing the subject
Mark 5: 1CA simplification (4,06)

subQuestions.questionText: The projected total gross value for 2022 was one hundred and eighteen billion, four hundred and five million US dollars. Write down this value using numerals (numbers).
subQuestions.memoText:
118 405 000 000 US$
Mark 1-2: 2A correct number (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Brazil has trade relationships with a number of countries. TABLE 5 shows the value (in billions of US$) of imports and exports for Brazil with six countries (China: 36,74/67,79; USA: 29,72/21,62; Germany: 9,68/4,12; Argentina: 8,22/8,49; South Korea: 4,66/3,76; Japan: 4,32/4,13). State the country with the smallest range between the imports and exports to Brazil.
subQuestions.memoText:
Japan (range = 4,32 - 4,13 = 0,19)
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct country (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the weakest currency against the Brazilian real. (Exchange rates: US$1 = BRL4,9642; 1BRL = R3,2026; €1 = BRL5,2379)
subQuestions.memoText:
ZAR / South African Rand / Rand
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct currency (2 marks)
(1 BRL = R3,2026, meaning 1 BRL gives 3,2026 ZAR; ZAR is weaker against BRL.)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the exchange rate between the euro and the South African rand in the form €1 = R...
subQuestions.memoText:
€1 = BRL 5,2379
€1 = 5,2379 × R3,2026 = R16,77489 / R16,77
Mark 1: 1RT correct rate
Mark 2: 1MCA multiplying correct values
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (R16,77)
NPR (min 2 decimal places). AO accepted.

subQuestions.questionText: Ludwig, a German citizen, stated that the difference between the United States imports and exports to Brazil is more than 7 600 million euros. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether Ludwig's statement is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
Difference (in US$) = 29,72 billion - 21,62 billion = 8,1 billion
Difference (in BRL) = 8,1 billion × 4,9642 = 40,21002 billion
Difference (in €) = 40,21002 ÷ 5,2379 = 7,676744497 billion = 7 676,744497 million
His statement is VALID (7 676,74 million > 7 600 million).
Mark 1: 1A difference in US$ (8,1 billion)
Mark 2: 1CA simplification
Mark 3: 1MCA multiplying by correct exchange rate
Mark 4: 1CA simplification (40,21002 billion)
Mark 5: 1CA answer in millions (7 676,744497 million)
Mark 6: 1O conclusion (VALID)
NPR
